URL: https://understandingwar.org/research/middle-east/iran-update-special-report-may-18-2026/
TITLE: Iran Update Special Report, May 18, 2026
PUBLISHED: 2026-05-18 23:26 UTC
AUTHOR: Stefaniia Bern (ISW/CTP)

KEY TAKEAWAYS:
1. Iran's latest counterproposal does not appear to meet US demands
   - Reuters: Iran sent new proposal with similar terms to ones previously rejected
   - Axios (senior US official + briefed source): Iran's counterproposal does not contain commitment "about suspending uranium enrichment or handing over its existing stockpile of highly enriched uranium (HEU)"
   - US considers proposal "insufficient"
   - IRGC media: "major disagreements" remain; Iran would never agree to "an end to the war in return for nuclear commitments"

2. TRUMP CANCELLED STRIKE PLANNED FOR MAY 19 (today)
   - Announced on Truth Social May 18
   - Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al Thani, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and Emirati President Mohamed bin Zayed asked Trump to suspend the strike "for two or three days" due to ongoing negotiations
   - US official + unspecified source told Axios: 3 Gulf leaders warned they would "pay the price" if US conducted new strikes
   - Concerns Iran would retaliate by targeting their energy and oil infrastructure
   - Gulf leaders believe US-Iran can reach deal "very acceptable to the United States" preventing Iran from getting nuclear weapons
   - Trump instructed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Chairman JCS General Dan Caine, US military to remain prepared to launch "full, large-scale assault" on short notice if negotiations fail

3. PERSIAN GULF STRAIT AUTHORITY (PGSA) — Iran formalising control
   - New Iranian regime body claims to be "legal institution and representative authority" for managing transit through Strait of Hormuz
   - Iran claims this is "legal" under UNCLOS — INCORRECT per ISW (Articles 37, 38, 44 of UNCLOS make Hormuz an international strait with right of transit passage; bordering states prohibited from "hampering" passage)
   - PGSA: navigation through designated zone requires "full coordination" with authority; transit without authorization "illegal"
   - Iranian state media: 1,500 vessels currently waiting for Iranian permission to transit strait

4. SUBSEA CABLES — IRGC threats
   - IRGC-affiliated Fars News: Iran could impose permits, oversight measures, sovereign fees on fiber-optic cables transiting strait
   - Major subsea cables: Asia-Africa-Europe 1 (AAE-1), FALCON, Gulf Bridge International Cable System
   - Three of seven cables (FALCON, GBICS, OMRAN/EPEG) connect to Iran via strait
   - IRGC-affiliated Javan News: simultaneous damage to several major subsea cables could cause widespread disruptions

MARITIME:
- CENTCOM May 18: 85 commercial vessels redirected, 4 disabled since April 13 blockade began
- 4 vessels redirected May 17 10am ET to May 18 1pm ET

ISRAEL-HEZBOLLAH:
- IDF May 18 announced airstrike Sunday near Baalbek killed PIJ Bekaa Valley operations commander Wael Mahmoud Abdel Halim
- Halim coordinated PIJ efforts to embed fighters into Hezbollah combat units and planned joint PIJ-Hezbollah attacks against Israeli forces in southern Lebanon
- Previous similar Israeli strikes: PIJ Al Quds Brigades commander Adham al Othman killed in Lebanon

OTHER AXIS:
- Saudi Defense Ministry: intercepted 3 drones launched from Iraq Sunday
- Iraqi MFA expressed "concern" about incident
- Iranian-backed Iraqi militia Kataib Hezbollah Spokesperson Abu Mujahid al Aasaf: militia will retaliate if renewed US/Israeli strikes on Iranian-backed Iraqi militias
- Claimed most US/Israeli "reconnaissance operations" originate from Jordan — warned Jordanian government
- Iranian-backed militias repeatedly attacked US bases in Jordan before ceasefire
